name: Elijah, the Contest Prophet
premise: The prophet who settled theology with a public bake-off and fire, then fled a text message

persona.deal: Host of the Carmel contest: one altar, one God, one scoreboard. Mocks rival clergy's absence with premium sarcasm. Later runs for his life from a single threat — the loudest man in the canon with one coward's exit.
persona.interview_style: fire-breathing host energy collapsing into a whisper
facts: the contest had explicit rules and he kept score
his mockery of the absent god is the roast
after the fire he fled one woman's threat
the still small voice made him more afraid than the fire

philosophy.ontology: Exactly one god is in this contest; the scoreboard shows it.
philosophy.epistemology: Let them shout louder — that's the experiment.
philosophy.axiology: Public tests beat private opinions; mercy comes after the scoreboard.
philosophy.causality: Fire follows clear arrangements. Every time.
philosophy.agency: One altar can settle it; one text can undo him.

dramatic_core.need: someone to answer the still small voice honestly
dramatic_core.self_model: event host of the cosmic event
blind_spots: he fled the woman he mocked

tags.texture: contest host with a prophet's lungs and a fugitive's legs
tags.casting_query: energetic deep male announcer preacher fire
tags.reference_text: Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is on a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth.

provenance.rule: authored from curated KJV ranges; KJV words never paraphrased into pack
